title: When the Bakery Burns
premise: Ivo Ashgrove, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter who writes novels under a pseudonym, joins an anonymous pen-pal program run by her small coastal town's library and is matched with the one man she can't forgive: Callum Vane, the fire investigator whose negligence ruling destroyed her family's bakery and her mother's reputation. Writing under assumed names, they fall for each other's words without knowing their identities, until Ivo discovers the truth and must decide whether her hatred was ever really about him. Digging into the fire, she uncovers evidence of arson insurance fraud implicating the town's beloved councilman, forcing her to choose between protecting her family's fragile peace and pursuing justice outside the law. In the end, she publishes the truth in her own name, clears her mother, and chooses Callum—risking the whole heart at last as the bakery rises from its ashes.
about_author: Ansel Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn romances about people who mistake duty for destiny.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeps Its Distance
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishing chapter: Ivo tends the decommissioned lighthouse her grandfather left her, writes romance novels under a pseudonym, and catalogs every reason love belongs in past tense. Her editor assigns her a local pen-pal column feature. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation beginning to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Fire investigator Callum Vane signs up for the library's anonymous pen-pal program on a colleague's dare, hoping to reconnect with something human after years of ash and blame. He writes his first letter honestly for the first time in years. Emotional beat: loneliness admitted on paper.

chapters.title: A Match Made by Mistake
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The librarian, rushing before closing, mismatches the envelopes: Ivo and Callum are paired despite the program's rule against townsfolk with known grievances. Neither recognizes the other's handwriting yet. First letters arrive—wry, guarded, unexpectedly alive. Emotional beat: spark without a name.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback woven through present: five years ago the Ashgrove Bakery burned; Callum's investigation ruled it electrical fault and operator negligence, branding Ivo's mother careless. Ivo answers her pen pal with borrowed warmth she doesn't give anyone in person. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into identity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Report
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. At a town meeting about rebuilding the harbor district, Callum sees Ivo across the room and feels the old case like a stone in his boot—he's never been certain the ruling was right. He writes his pen pal something dangerously true. Emotional beat: doubt as the first crack in certainty.

chapters.title: Ink Before Coffee
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The correspondence deepens; her pen pal asks questions no one else does, and her stalled novel starts moving again. She almost tells him about the bakery, then deflects. Meanwhile Callum, unrecognized, buys bread from her market stall and they argue about rye versus sourdough. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in two directions at once.

chapters.title: Ash Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Reassigned to review cold cases ahead of an audit, Callum pulls the Ashgrove file and finds gaps: a missing accelerant test, a witness statement never followed up. He begins quietly reinvestigating. He tells his pen pal he once ruined someone. Emotional beat: guilt seeking a shape.

chapters.title: The Councilman's Generosity
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Councilman Aldous Pemberton, the bakery's former landlord, makes a public show of funding the harbor rebuild—and Ivo notices his insurance payout records don't match his public losses. A throwaway line in her pen-pal letter about rich men and fires gets an oddly urgent reply. Emotional beat: suspicion kindling.

chapters.title: Almost, Nearly, Not Quite
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A near-miss reveal: Ivo finds one of Callum's letters in his coat at the market stall and assumes he has another pen pal; Callum glimpses Ivo's manuscript pages and realizes her prose voice is familiar from somewhere he can't place. Both retreat. Emotional beat: jealousy and recognition circling each other.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Rereading her pen pal's early letters, Ivo recognizes a phrase—a fire-investigator's idiom her mother used to mock from the report. She matches the handwriting to the signature on the ruling that ruined them. Her pen pal is Callum Vane. Emotional beat: betrayal detonating in slow motion.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Furious, Ivo drafts a cruel final letter, then stops—because his latest letter contains his confession that he's reopening her family's case. She writes back as a stranger still, testing whether the man in the letters and the man in the report can be the same. Emotional beat: hatred and hope refusing to separate.

chapters.title: Cold Case, Warm Hands
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum interviews the retired volunteer firefighter who first responded and learns Pemberton's car was seen near the bakery that night. He requests the sealed insurance documents and warns his pen pal that the truth will implicate powerful people. Emotional beat: duty realigning toward justice.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Table
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Forced together by the harbor committee, Ivo and Callum work late over maps of the old district. Off-duty honesty leaks through; they nearly kiss, and Ivo pulls away, unable to reconcile the man beside her with the name in her head. Emotional beat: longing at war with loyalty.

chapters.title: The Letter She Shouldn't Send
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reveals herself to Callum by mail—signing her real name for the first time—and lays out everything: the bakery, her mother, the years of shame. Then she waits, sick with dread, for the man behind the report to answer. Emotional beat: the whole heart placed on the table.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum comes to the lighthouse at dawn, having guessed the address from her return postmark long ago. He admits his original investigation was pressured to close quickly—and hands her copies of everything he's found on Pemberton. Emotional beat: accountability offered without excuse.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and Callum build the case together: altered lease terms, a doubled insurance policy taken weeks before the fire, a payoff to the volunteer department's silence. But going public means accusing the town's benefactor with no legal standing—and Pemberton learns they're asking questions. Emotional beat: fear and resolve burning side by side.

chapters.title: Pressure Drop
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Pemberton strikes: Callum is suspended pending an ethics review, the library pen-pal archive is seized, and Ivo's landlord suddenly terminates her market lease. Her mother begs her to let it go. Ivo realizes staying invisible is exactly what Pemberton is counting on. Emotional beat: the cost of justice made concrete.

chapters.title: Everything Flammable
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered, Ivo chooses her weapon: she finishes the novel she's been writing all along—a thinly veiled account of the fire—and decides to publish it under her own name, with the documentary evidence appended. Callum, suspended but not silent, secures a sworn statement from the retired firefighter. Emotional beat: invisibility surrendered on purpose.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the harbor festival, Ivo reads the opening chapters publicly; the crowd that came for entertainment stays for the truth. The retired firefighter stands and swears his statement aloud. Pemberton's composure cracks on camera. Callum takes Ivo's hand in front of everyone. Emotional beat: the climax—truth spoken where it cannot be unsaid.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Arson Charges
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. State investigators reopen the case; Pemberton is charged with arson and fraud, and Callum's suspension is lifted with an apology. Ivo's mother, cleared in the public record, visits the lighthouse and finally embraces her daughter's choices. Emotional beat: vindication arriving quieter than expected.

chapters.title: Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Spring: the community rebuilds the bakery as a co-op, and Ivo signs her published novel at its opening. She and Callum are learning each other un-anonymized—awkward, honest, real. Her next book's dedication page names him. Emotional beat: love in present tense, chosen daily.

chapters.title: When the Bakery Burns
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. One year later, a small kitchen fire—pure accident—sends the town into brief panic, and Ivo and Callum laugh until they cry in the smoke-smelling doorway, holding each other. The lighthouse beam turns overhead. Final beat: what burns can be rebuilt when you stop keeping score and start keeping faith.
